questions.question:
In the Rabin-Karp algorithm, the hashing technique is used to:
a) store the string
b) calculate the matching of substrings
c) compare every substring
d) search for substrings by calculating hash values

options.D: search for substrings by calculating hash values

questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp hashes every window of length m and compares hash values first, verifying characters only when the hashes agree. That makes the search fast on average.

questions.question:
The Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) string matching algorithm preprocesses the pattern to:
a) avoid rechecking the matched characters
b) compare characters from the end
c) skip unmatched characters entirely
d) directly match the substring
questions.explanation: KMP preprocesses the pattern into an LPS (failure) array, so after a mismatch it knows how far to shift without re-checking characters that already matched.

questions.question:
What is a Rabin and Karp Algorithm?
a) String Matching Algorithm
b) Shortest Path Algorithm
c) Spanning Tree Algorithm
d) Approximation Algorithm
questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp is a string matching algorithm that uses a rolling hash to locate a pattern inside a text in average O(n+m) time.

questions.question:
What is a Rabin and Karp Algorithm?
a) String Matching Algorithm
b) Shortest Path Algorithm
c) Minimum spanning tree Algorithm
d) Approximation Algorithm
questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp belongs to string matching: it hashes the pattern and each text window to find occurrences, and can search for several patterns at once.

What is the worst-case time complexity of the Naive (Brute Force) String Matching algorithm?
a) O(n)
b) O(m)
c) O(n × m)
d) O(n + m)
questions.explanation: The naive algorithm tries the pattern at each of about n starting positions and may compare m characters at each, so the worst case is O(n × m).

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of the KMP string matching algorithm?
a) O(n × m)
b) O(n + m)
c) O(n²)
d) O(m²)
questions.explanation: KMP builds the LPS array in O(m) and then scans the text once in O(n), giving O(n + m) overall with no backtracking in the text.

questions.question:
What is the worst-case time complexity of the Rabin-Karp algorithm?
a) O(n + m)
b) O(n × m)
c) O(n log m)
d) O(m²)
questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp averages O(n + m), but if many windows share the pattern's hash each is verified character by character, giving O(n × m) worst case.

questions.question:
Horspool's string matching algorithm compares the pattern with text in which direction?
a) Left to right
b) Right to left
c) From the middle outward
d) Random order
questions.explanation: Horspool compares the window from right to left, starting at its last character, and shifts using a bad-character table. That right-to-left scan is its signature.

questions.question:
The Boyer-Moore string matching algorithm uses which of the following heuristics?
a) Bad character heuristic only
b) Good suffix heuristic only
c) Both bad character and good suffix heuristics
d) Rolling hash function

options.C: Both bad character and good suffix heuristics

questions.explanation: Boyer-Moore combines the bad-character and good-suffix heuristics and shifts by the larger of the two, which skips many alignments at once.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity to search for a word of length L in a Trie?
a) O(n)
b) O(L)
c) O(n × L)
d) O(log n)
questions.explanation: A trie consumes one character per level, so finding a word of length L costs O(L) regardless of how many words are stored.

questions.question:
Which sorting algorithm is most commonly used for sorting strings?
a) Quick Sort
b) Merge Sort
c) MSD Radix Sort
d) Bubble Sort
questions.explanation: MSD radix sort partitions strings by their first character and then recursively by later characters, which suits variable-length strings. It is the standard choice here.

questions.question:
In regular expressions, the symbol '*' (Kleene star) means:
a) Exactly one occurrence of the preceding element
b) Zero or more occurrences of the preceding element
c) One or more occurrences of the preceding element
d) Optional occurrence of the preceding element

options.A: Exactly one occurrence of the preceding element
options.B: Zero or more occurrences of the preceding element
options.C: One or more occurrences of the preceding element
options.D: Optional occurrence of the preceding element

questions.explanation: In regular expressions * means zero or more repetitions of the preceding element, while + means one or more and ? means at most one.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a lossless data compression technique?
a) JPEG compression
b) MP3 compression
c) Huffman Coding
d) Video streaming compression
questions.explanation: Huffman coding gives short bit codes to frequent characters and longer codes to rare ones without losing information, so it is a lossless method.

The Rabin-Karp algorithm uses which technique to efficiently compute hash values for successive substrings?
a) Static hashing
b) Rolling hash
c) Double hashing
d) Universal hashing
questions.explanation: A rolling hash updates the window hash in O(1) by removing the outgoing character and adding the incoming one, so each shift costs constant time.

questions.question:
In the KMP algorithm, if the pattern is P = "AABAAC", what is the LPS (failure function) array?
a) [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
b) [0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 0]
c) [0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2]
d) [0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3]
questions.explanation: For AABAAC the LPS values are 0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 0: at position 4 the prefix AA matches the suffix AA, and the final C extends nothing. That is option B.

What is the best-case time complexity of the Boyer-Moore string matching algorithm?
a) O(n × m)
b) O(n + m)
c) O(n / m)
d) O(n)
questions.explanation: The best case is O(n/m), because a mismatch on the last character lets the algorithm jump a whole pattern length. The worst case remains O(n × m).

questions.question:
Horspool's algorithm is a simplified version of which algorithm?
a) KMP Algorithm
b) Rabin-Karp Algorithm
c) Boyer-Moore Algorithm
d) Naive String Matching
questions.explanation: Horspool simplifies Boyer-Moore by keeping only the bad-character shift rule applied to the window's last character, which is easier to implement.

Run-Length Encoding (RLE) is most effective on data with:
a) Completely random characters
b) Many unique characters
c) Long runs of repeated characters
d) Short strings only
questions.explanation: RLE stores a repeated character once with a count, so it shrinks data containing long runs, such as flat image regions. Random data can even grow.
